- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially +1.00) — reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices during sentiment downturns (especially -1.00 or 0.00) — add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion.
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 3–5 day delays) are overpredicted — adjust forecast to align with 2–4 day lagged true values.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes — cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment +0.00 periods: forecast should be closer to 30-day moving average — avoid overbidding.
- High sentiment +0.40 or +0.00 with no prior spike: reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Forecast horizon >14 days: reduce slope of upward trend — avoid exponential growth assumptions.
- If sentiment history shows 2+ consecutive 0.00s, apply 1–2% downward bias to avoid false optimism.
